architecturalPlan.thesis: A single-storey waterfront estate conceived as a deeply shaded limestone-and-ivory belvedere: a tall central social hall mediates between a deliberately compressed landward arrival court and a broad south-facing pool terrace, while two long, quiet bedroom cloisters extend laterally as sheltered private arms. The composition makes the waterfront elevation a layered sequence of solid service piers, deep veranda shadow and living-room glazing rather than an indiscriminate glass wall.

constraints.reason: The paired cloisters must remain materially and acoustically separated by the substantial social pavilion.
The estate concept depends on a broad, operable indoor-outdoor living threshold.
A generous sun deck and circulation band is preserved between shade and water.
